channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President departs for Kyrgyzstan to attend SCO summit and related meetings
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has traveled to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting and an SCO plus format meeting. Discussions will focus on SCO development and regional cooperation, with bilateral meetings also planned.

item.title: Bishkek hosts SCO summit and state visits with unprecedented security measures
item.description: Bishkek is hosting the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit and official visits from heads of state on August 31 and September 1. The city expects 21 presidents and prime ministers, leading to unprecedented security measures. The SCO celebrates its 25th anniversary, with the summit of heads of state and observer countries scheduled for September 1. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a video of a performer reciting from the Manas epic.

item.title: Armenian PM Pashinyan met with Azerbaijani President Aliyev in Bishkek
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Bishkek, as announced by Pashinyan on social media. The leaders arrived in Kyrgyzstan to participate in a high-level meeting in the "SCO plus" format and the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. Details of the meeting and discussed issues have not yet been disclosed.

item.title: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev arrives in Kyrgyzstan for working visit
item.description: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev and his wife, Mehriban Aliyeva, have arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. They were welcomed at Manas International Airport by Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. President Aliyev was presented with a snow leopard toy, the mascot of the 6th World Nomad Games. Kyrgyzstan holds the SCO presidency in 2026.

item.title: Afghanistan poses no threat to neighboring countries, says Taliban representative
item.description: Zabihullah Mujahid, a representative of Afghanistan's interim government, responded to statements by Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) Secretary General Taalatbek Masadikov regarding arms and equipment supplies to the Tajikistan-Afghanistan border. Mujahid stated Afghanistan does not threaten its neighbors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan views Togo as a promising partner in Africa
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with Togo's Prime Minister on August 31, viewing Togo as a promising partner on the African continent. Japarov thanked Togo for supporting Kyrgyzstan's candidacy for the UN Security Council. Togo expressed interest in expanding trade and cultural cooperation.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon visits Kyrgyzstan for working trip
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Kyrgyzstan on August 31 for a working visit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Adylbek Kasymaliev. Rahmon received a stuffed snow leopard toy, the national symbol and mascot of the World Nomad Games. Kyrgyzstan will chair the SCO in 2026 and host its anniversary summit this year.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev arrives in Bishkek with spouse for SCO summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Adylbek Kasymaliev. Mirziyoyev will attend the SCO heads of state council meeting, a high-level meeting in the "SCO plus" format, and the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. He received a snow leopard toy, the national symbol and mascot of the games.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev travels to Bishkek for SCO meeting
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has departed for Bishkek on a working visit. He will attend the upcoming meeting of the Council of SCO Heads of State and a "SCO Plus" format meeting on August 31.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Calls US Economic War Against Tehran a "Failed Policy"
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described US President Donald Trump's threat to launch an economic war against Tehran as a "continuation of Washington's failed policies." Araghchi's remarks were made in response to Trump's threats.

item.title: Yerlan Karin Appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree appointing Yerlan Karin as the country's Vice President. Karin's candidacy was previously approved by the Parliament, with 141 out of 145 deputies supporting his appointment.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the SCO Heads of State Summit. He was welcomed at the airport by Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev and other officials. The presidential press service reported on the arrival.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New Funding Rules for Private Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education proposes new fixed funding rules for private schools that teach children under the state order. The ministry suggests maintaining a constant funding amount, unaffected by annual increases in the monthly calculated indicator (MRP), to ensure educational accessibility and stability.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Infrastructure Development Fund as Treasury Account
item.description: Kazakhstan's government has established the Infrastructure Development Fund as a special account within the state treasury, rather than a separate organization. This fund will finance major national infrastructure projects, with payments disbursed in stages based on work completion.

item.title: China, Kazakhstan, and Russia Discuss Arctic Access via Irtysh River Corridor
item.description: China, Kazakhstan, and Russia are exploring a project to transform the Irtysh River into a cargo corridor connecting to the Arctic. This "Water Silk Road" aims to bypass traditional maritime routes vulnerable to blockade, offering a strategic alternative for transporting goods from China.

item.title: First Direct Flight from Dushanbe to Minsk Celebrated with Water Arch Ceremony
item.description: Minsk National Airport welcomed the first direct flight from Dushanbe with a traditional water arch ceremony. The new Somon Air route, launched in honor of Tajikistan's 35th Independence Day, aims to strengthen relations, boost tourism, and facilitate trade between Tajikistan and Belarus.

item.title: Two Dead After Pleasure Boat Crashes into Rock Face in Aktau
item.description: A pleasure boat carrying seven people collided with a rock face in the Caspian Sea near Aktau, resulting in two fatalities. Rescuers recovered five survivors and the bodies of two individuals who were reportedly not wearing life jackets. Investigations into the cause of the accident are underway.

item.title: New rules for handling archaeological finds in Kazakhstan require preservation for three years
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced new regulations for archaeologists on how to store, process, and transfer excavated artifacts like bones, pottery, and metal objects to the state. The rules prohibit cleaning artifacts with household chemicals or drying them by fire. Metal items must be extracted with soil to prevent damage.

item.title: Repressions in Central Asia: Purge quotas and fate of women and children revealed
item.description: Documents reveal NKVD quotas for repression in Central Asia, targeting 224,400 individuals for execution or imprisonment. Uzbekistan SSR was allocated 4,750 cases: 750 for execution and 4,000 for imprisonment.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon travels to Bishkek for SCO summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon departed for Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the summit of heads of state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). He was seen off by high-ranking officials at Dushanbe International Airport.

item.title: Kazakhstan mining firms can adjust procurement costs due to weak tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Industry and Construction allows solid mineral mining companies to recalculate procurement costs based on the tenge's exchange rate. This applies to contracts signed before or during payment.

item.title: Russia's Defense Ministry announces plans for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy sector
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Defense stated on August 30 that the armed forces are preparing massive strikes against Ukraine's energy facilities. These actions are described as a response to alleged Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and its fuel-energy complex.

item.title: Uzbekistan's UN Resident Coordinator reflects on two years of changes and climate challenges
item.description: Akiko Fujii, UN Development Programme Resident Representative in Uzbekistan, reflects on two years in the country. She highlights climate change impacts, noting over 25% of land is degraded and 45% faces desertification risk, emphasizing the importance of water reforms.

item.title: US strikes Iranian missile launchers; Tehran targets US bases in Jordan
item.description: On August 30, US forces attacked Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, Iran reportedly launched missile strikes against US military bases 'King Hussein' and 'Al-Azraq' in Jordan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Appoints New Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan. The decree was signed by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Aripov replaces Erlan Abdildaev, who was previously released from this post and appointed Ambassador to Hungary.

item.title: UN Secretary-General António Guterres Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has arrived in Kyrgyzstan to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Minister of Economy and Commerce, Bakyt Sydykov. Guterres will attend the Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek.

item.title: 12 Uzbek children without parental care returned from Russia
item.description: Twelve underage Uzbek citizens, deprived of parental care or in difficult social situations, have been returned to Uzbekistan from various regions of Russia. The repatriation was a collaborative effort involving the Uzbek embassy, ministries of internal affairs and health, and the National Agency for Social Protection. This year, 38 children have been repatriated from Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day. Mirziyoyev noted Kyrgyzstan's economic and social growth under Japarov's leadership and highlighted the elevated bilateral relations to a "union level." He also emphasized the importance of regional cooperation and upcoming events.

item.title: Hong Kong banks may finance Tashkent-Samarkand toll road project
item.description: Hong Kong banks are considering financing the construction of the Tashkent-Samarkand toll road. The potential involvement of Hong Kong financial institutions was discussed by Uzbekistan's Transport Minister Ilkhom Makhkamov and the head of Hong Kong's "Belt and Road" Office, Nicholas Ho Lik-chi. Prospects for air travel and economic cooperation were also discussed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker congratulates nation on Independence Day
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, congratulated Kyrgyzstan's citizens on the 35th anniversary of Independence. He emphasized that strengthening independence is a duty and highlighted the country's progress in economic, state, and international spheres under President Sadyr Japarov. The Speaker wished for peace, unity, and prosperity.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Secretary Links Xi Jinping's Visit to Ancient Monk's Journey
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Arslan Koichiev drew a historical parallel between Xi Jinping's visit and the 7th-century monk Xuanzang's journey. Koichiev noted Xi's visit to the same location Xuanzang stayed and referenced Xi's article on Kyrgyzstan-China relations, highlighting historical figures who fostered cultural exchange.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Asked US to Lead Anti-Houthi War, Washington Refused
item.description: Saudi Arabia requested the United States to lead a war against the Houthis, but Washington declined. This issue was raised during a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Admiral Brad Cooper, head of the US Central Command, on August 14.

item.title: US President Trump Congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: US President Donald Trump sent congratulations to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on their Independence Day. He highlighted the strong relationship built on mutual respect, economic ties, and shared commitment to regional security. The US reaffirms its support for Kyrgyzstan's sovereignty and independence.

item.title: Leaders of Several Countries Congratulate Kyrgyzstan on 35th Independence Anniversary
item.description: Heads of state from Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Belgium, Iran, Pakistan, Egypt, Belarus, Azerbaijan, and Turkey, along with Armenia's Prime Minister, congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its 35th Independence Day. They wished the nation peace and prosperity and President Japarov good health and success. Several leaders expressed eagerness to deepen bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh President: Kyrgyzstan Has Successfully Developed Since Independence
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day, noting its growing authority, evidenced by its UN Security Council election. He highlighted reforms for economic growth and praised the fraternal relations between Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organization Celebrates 25 Years, Drives Regional Economic Cooperation
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) marks its 25th anniversary, having grown into a major international body with 27 member states and a GDP nearing $30 trillion. The SCO actively promotes trade, energy, transport, and digital economy projects, enhancing regional stability and global governance.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Bishkek for State Visit and SCO Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife were welcomed in Bishkek by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Xi Jinping conveyed greetings to the Kyrgyz people, highlighting the long-standing friendship and stable development of bilateral relations, now at a high level of comprehensive partnership.

item.title: Britain warns companies supplying arms to Ukraine about Russian attack risks
item.description: British government officials have informed defense company leaders about increased threats from the Kremlin against them and their staff. This warning comes as companies supply arms to Ukraine, highlighting potential Russian attack risks.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island; Iran retaliates against US bases in Jordan
item.description: The US conducted strikes on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting forces preparing to mine the strait. Iran's IRGC claimed to have retaliated by striking two US military bases in Jordan, targeting infrastructure and fighter jets.

item.title: New Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway shows significant damage after construction
item.description: Activists report significant damage to the new Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway, including asphalt degradation and foundation issues, less than two years after its completion. The road, built with Chinese loans, cost over 180 billion tenge and has a two-year warranty.
